note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in LA.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: San Bernardo Byway
byways.where: LA 46 and connecting roads from the New Orleans line through Arabi and Chalmette to Shell Beach, St. Bernard Parish

facts.fact: The byway follows Highway 46 for 36 miles from just east of New Orleans to Shell Beach in St. Bernard Parish.
Chalmette National Historic Park and Battlefield, site of the 1815 Battle of New Orleans, is on the route.
Los Islenos Museum and Village has six museum homes showing the heritage of the Isleños, settlers from the Canary Islands.

byways.review: Catalog line is about 15 mi and stops well short of Shell Beach (bbox east edge -89.89); DOTD layer value 'San Bernardo Byway' covers the whole route to about -89.64 and should replace it.

byways.name: Creole Nature Trail All-American Road
byways.where: LA 27 and LA 82 with connecting roads from Sulphur and Lake Charles south to Holly Beach, Cameron and Grand Chenier; Calcasieu and Cameron parishes

facts.fact: The 180-mile drive passes four wildlife refuges and 26 miles of natural Gulf beaches.
Cheniers, sandy ridges studded with oaks, rise above the coastal lowlands along the route.
Peveto Woods Sanctuary is a 41-acre stopover used by about two million birds a year.

byways.review: DOTD layer value is 'Creole Nature Trail All-American Road'; catalog line matches it closely (99% overlap).

byways.name: Cajun Corridor Byway
byways.where: LA 14 from Gueydan through Kaplan and Abbeville to Delcambre, Vermilion Parish

facts.fact: The byway runs 34 miles on Highway 14 from Gueydan to Delcambre in Vermilion Parish.
C.S. Steen Syrup Mill in Abbeville has made pure cane syrup since about 1910.
Delcambre is a shrimping town whose boat docks are a stop on the byway.

byways.review: The catalog's Jean Lafitte Scenic Byway (an older, larger route) includes this stretch of LA 14; 25% of its line is Cajun Corridor.

byways.name: Myths and Legends Byway
byways.where: LA 8, LA 111, US 190 and connecting roads from Burr Ferry through Merryville, DeRidder and Sugartown; Vernon, Beauregard and Allen parishes

facts.fact: The 181-mile byway crosses a region once called No Man's Land for its disputed boundaries and lawless past, first home to the Atakapa and Coushatta and later a refuge for pirates and outlaws.
Civil War breastworks survive at Burr Ferry, where the byway begins at LA 8 and LA 111.
DeRidder has a Gothic Revival jail that is now open for tours.

byways.review: Matched to the catalog's Attakapas-Coushatta Scenic Byway, which appears to be the earlier name, but the catalog line is only US 190 Merryville to DeRidder (23 mi). DOTD value 'Myths and Legends Byway' gives the full network (about 173 mi) and should replace it.

byways.name: Longleaf Trail Byway
byways.designation: Louisiana Scenic Byway (also a National Forest Scenic Byway)
byways.where: Forest Road 59 between LA 117 and LA 119, Kisatchie National Forest

facts.fact: The byway runs 17 miles on Forest Road 59 between Highway 117 and Highway 119 in the Kisatchie National Forest.
Elevations range from 80 to 400 feet, with mesas, buttes, sandstone outcrops and longleaf pines in view from outlooks.
The Kisatchie Hills Wilderness beside the road is known locally as the Little Grand Canyon; Longleaf Vista has overlooks four miles west of Highway 119.

byways.review: DOTD value 'Longleaf Trail Byway'; catalog line matches it fully.

byways.name: Flyway Byway
byways.where: US 90, LA 14, LA 26 and LA 99 in a loop through Jennings, Welsh and Lake Arthur, Jefferson Davis Parish

facts.fact: The 55-mile byway passes rice fields and crawfish ponds in southwest Louisiana.
More than 160 bird species are found along the route, and Lacassine National Wildlife Refuge and the Lake Arthur park and boardwalk are on it.
The loop runs through Welsh, Jennings and Lake Arthur on US 90, LA 14, LA 26 and LA 99.

byways.review: The program page calls it part of the Louisiana Scenic Byways program; the WebFetch summary also said 'National Scenic Byway', but Scenic America's 2023 list and the 2021 designations show it as a state byway only. Part of the catalog's Jean Lafitte line overlaps it.

byways.name: Boom or Bust National Scenic Byway
byways.where: LA 2 from the Texas line and LA 3049 east to Lake Claiborne, with loops at each end; Caddo, Bossier, Webster and Claiborne parishes

facts.fact: The byway follows Highway 2 between the Louisiana-Texas border and Highway 3049 on the west and Lake Claiborne on the east, across Caddo, Bossier, Webster and Claiborne parishes.
It tells of booms and busts in oil and gas, lumber, transportation, farming and entertainment; graveyards of old oilfield equipment line parts of the route.
Stops include Oil City, the Louisiana State Oil & Gas Museum, Caddo Lake and the Germantown Colony museum.
It was designated a National Scenic Byway in February 2021.

byways.review: Matched to the catalog's Northwest Louisiana Scenic Byway, the older and larger (237 mi) route in the same corridor; only about half its line is Boom or Bust. DOTD value 'Boom or Bust' should replace it.

byways.name: Louisiana River Road – All-American Road
byways.where: Great River Road along the Mississippi from opposite Vicksburg south past Baton Rouge and the river parishes to New Orleans

facts.fact: The Louisiana Great River Road was designated an All-American Road in February 2021.
The program lists the route at 773 miles, entering Louisiana opposite Vicksburg and running to New Orleans.
Attractions include the Louisiana State Capitol, Frogmore Cotton Plantation and Gins, Oak Alley, Whitney Plantation and the French Quarter.

byways.review: Matched to the multi-state Great River Road (2279), whose catalog designations lack the 2021 All-American Road status for Louisiana. The catalog also has river-road-scenic-byway-2075, an older Louisiana-only line of the same road (80% on DOTD 'Great River Road'); treat it as a duplicate. DOTD value 'Great River Road' gives the state's own line.

byways.name: Historic US 80
byways.designation: Louisiana Scenic Byway (Historic US 80 / Dixie Overland)
byways.where: US 80 from Ruston through Monroe to the Mississippi River at Delta, opposite Vicksburg

facts.fact: The state named a 105-mile stretch of US 80 from Ruston to the Mississippi state line the Historic US 80 Byway, through farm and forest country used by farmers and loggers.
The route ends at the Mississippi River opposite Vicksburg.
Monroe stops include the Biedenharn Museum and Gardens with its Coca-Cola museum, and the Chennault Aviation and Military Museum, which covers Delta Air Lines history.

byways.review: The program page gives both 105 and 113 miles. The catalog's Bienville Trace (an older 566-mi network in northeast Louisiana) contains US 80 from Ruston to Tallulah but is not this byway.

byways.name: Zydeco Cajun Prairie Scenic Byway
byways.where: Three loops and a spur through Opelousas, Eunice, Mamou, Ville Platte, Crowley, Washington and Grand Coteau; St. Landry, Acadia and Evangeline parishes

facts.fact: The 283-mile byway is three loops plus a spur through St. Landry, Acadia and Evangeline parishes, past crawfish farms, sweet potato fields and cattle pasture.
Fred's Lounge on the route is known for Saturday morning Cajun music and dancing.
Crowley's Historic Rice Theatre and Chicot State Park, 6,400 acres, are on the byway.

byways.name: Toledo Bend Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: LA 191 along Toledo Bend Reservoir between Logansport and the dam; Sabine and DeSoto parishes

facts.fact: The 78-mile byway follows Toledo Bend Reservoir, the largest manmade lake in the South, through pine and hardwood forest on the Texas border.
The route follows LA 191 along the reservoir.
South Toledo Bend State Park sits on bluffs and is known for bass fishing and nesting bald eagles; Logansport's riverfront is at the northern end.

byways.review: Catalog line is 355 mi and mostly other roads (overlaps Colonial Trails and Myths and Legends; only 23% is the current byway). DOTD value 'Toledo Bend Byway' (about 77 mi) should replace it.

byways.name: Cane River National Heritage Trail Scenic Byway
byways.where: LA 1, LA 119 and LA 494 along Cane River from Natchitoches to Cloutierville, with LA 6 and LA 485 toward Allen; Natchitoches Parish

facts.fact: Cane River, once a main channel of the Red River, is now an oxbow lake bordered by corn and soybean farms, sugar cane and pecan orchards.
The byway runs from Natchitoches, the oldest permanent settlement in the Louisiana Purchase, to Cloutierville.
Cane River Creole National Historical Park takes in Oakland and part of Magnolia plantations, and St. Augustine Catholic Church was the first built and supported by free people of color.

byways.review: The catalog's Colonial Trails line overlaps parts of this route but is not it.

byways.name: Bayou Teche National Scenic Byway
byways.where: LA 182, LA 31 and other roads along both sides of Bayou Teche from Morgan City to Arnaudville, with a loop through Catahoula; St. Mary, Iberia and St. Martin parishes

facts.fact: The byway runs from Morgan City through Franklin, New Iberia, St. Martinville and Breaux Bridge to Arnaudville, following Bayou Teche west of the Atchafalaya Basin.
Stops include the Chitimacha Indian Reservation and Museum and Shadows-on-the-Teche in New Iberia.
It was designated a National Scenic Byway in February 2021.

byways.review: Catalog line is 310 mi against the program's 183; 68% lies on DOTD 'Bayou Teche Byway'. The catalog's Promised Land Scenic Byway is 72% on the same DOTD feature (the St. Martin Parish roads around Catahoula) and looks absorbed into this byway.

byways.name: Southern Swamp Byway
byways.where: LA 22 and old US 51 from Sorrento through Springfield, Ponchatoula and Manchac to LaPlace; Ascension, Livingston and Tangipahoa parishes

facts.fact: The 69-mile byway runs from Sorrento to LaPlace through Ascension, Livingston and Tangipahoa parishes.
It crosses the Maurepas and Manchac swamps on old US 51 and LA 22.
Joyce Wildlife Management Area has an elevated boardwalk through the swamp, and Middendorf's restaurant is known for catfish.

byways.review: Wikipedia and DOTD spell it 'Southern Swamps Byway'; the program site says 'Southern Swamp Byway'. The catalog's older Louisiana Scenic Bayou Byway overlaps part of it.

byways.name: Wetlands Cultural Trail
byways.where: LA 1 along Bayou Lafourche from Raceland to Port Fourchon and Grand Isle; LA 56 and LA 57 south of Houma; LA 24 Houma to Thibodaux; Lafourche and Terrebonne parishes

facts.fact: The route follows Highway 1 from Raceland to Port Fourchon, Highways 56 and 57 from Houma to the Gulf, and Highway 24 between Houma and Thibodaux.
Families in its towns have shrimped, trapped and farmed for centuries.
Stops include Grand Isle State Park, the Louisiana Universities Marine Consortium at Cocodrie and the Bayou Lafourche Folklife & Heritage Museum in Lockport.

byways.review: DOTD value is 'Wetlands Cultural Byway'; catalog line is 82% on it.

byways.name: Zachary Taylor Parkway
byways.where: Bogalusa to Pineville via Franklinton, Clinton, St. Francisville, New Roads, Marksville and Alexandria

facts.fact: The 203-mile byway connects Bogalusa to Pineville, crossing three other Louisiana byways.
It honors Zachary Taylor's service in the War of 1812 and the Mexican-American War; Baton Rouge was his adopted home.
Points of interest include the John James Audubon Bridge, the Clinton courthouse and Lawyer's Row, and Forts Randolph and Buhlow.

byways.review: Not in the catalog. The older Louisiana Scenic Bayou Byway line shares LA 1 and other roads with it (30% overlap).

byways.name: Northup Trail
byways.where: Roads along Bayou Boeuf from Alexandria through Bunkie to Marksville; Rapides and Avoyelles parishes

facts.fact: Solomon Northup, a free-born musician from New York, was kidnapped in 1841 and enslaved in central Louisiana for twelve years; his memoir Twelve Years a Slave became an Oscar-winning film.
The 83-mile trail runs from Alexandria, where he landed at the Red River, to Marksville.
At the Avoyelles Parish courthouse in Marksville his freedom was legally established on January 4, 1853.

byways.review: Program gives 83 miles, Wikipedia 123; DOTD line is about 67 mi (134 counting both directions).

byways.name: Louisiana Colonial Trails
byways.where: US 84, LA 6, LA 8, LA 28 and other highways across central Louisiana, Texas line to the Mississippi opposite Natchez

facts.fact: The byway follows LA 6 from the Texas state line to Clarence and US 84 from Clarence to the Mississippi state line at Natchez, among other highways.
Its network includes parts of the Old San Antonio Road and El Camino Real and runs 484 miles.

byways.review: NOT listed on the program site today (its old page /byway/louisiana-colonial-trails-byway returns 403 like a missing page), but it is in Scenic America's 2023 list of 19, still active in the DOTD layer (value 'Colonial Trails', edited 2020, no end date) and named as a byway on the program's own Zachary Taylor Parkway page. Kept as a member pending a human check.

byways.name: Tunica Trace Byway
byways.where: LA 66 from US 61 north of St. Francisville to the Louisiana State Penitentiary at Angola, West Feliciana Parish

facts.fact: LA 66 runs 19.6 miles from the main entrance of the Louisiana State Penitentiary at Angola to US 61 north of St. Francisville.
The highway winds through the Tunica Hills and follows an ancient Native American portage known as the Tunica Trace.
It crosses Bayou Sara on a pony truss bridge from the 1940s.

byways.review: NOT listed on the program site today (old page /byway/tunica-trace-byway returns 403), but in Scenic America's 2023 list of 19 and still in the DOTD layer (value 'Tunica Trace', no end date). Kept as a member pending a human check.

issues: Program site (byways.explorelouisiana.com) returns 403 to curl and to WebFetch for removed pages; existing pages were read through WebFetch summaries, so spellings and numbers should be spot-checked in a browser.

Louisiana Colonial Trails and Tunica Trace are missing from the program site's list of 17 but appear in Scenic America's 2023 list of 19 and remain active in the DOTD layer; the Zachary Taylor Parkway page still calls Colonial Trails a byway. I kept both as members with notes. Decide whether to show them.

Several catalog lines are older or larger routes than today's byways and should be replaced by DOTD lines: Toledo Bend Forest (355 mi vs 78), Northwest Louisiana for Boom or Bust (237 vs 137), Attakapas-Coushatta for Myths and Legends (23 vs 181), San Bernardo (15 mi, stops short of Shell Beach).

Six catalog roads (Bienville Trace, Jean Lafitte, Louisiana Scenic Bayou, Promised Land, The Real French Destination, River Road 2075) are not in today's program; listed under a 'former' group with no blurbs. Consider hiding them, and treat river-road-scenic-byway-2075 as a duplicate of the Great River Road.

Great River Road (2279) catalog designations lack Louisiana's 2021 All-American Road status; Bayou Teche (2066) and Northwest Louisiana/Boom or Bust (2068) catalog entries lack their 2021 National Scenic Byway status.
Mileage disagreements: Historic US 80 page says both 105 and 113 miles; Northup Trail is 83 miles on the program site and 123 on Wikipedia.
Longleaf Trail is also a USFS National Forest Scenic Byway in the catalog; it is the same road, so it is not repeated as a separate USFS program.

Left out of the chapter: Former Louisiana Scenic Byways (older routes no longer in the program): Bienville Trace Scenic Byway, Jean Lafitte Scenic Byway, Louisiana Scenic Bayou Byway, Promised Land Scenic Byway, The Real French Destination Scenic Byway, River Road Scenic Byway
